aperture.label: Cloud gateway (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint with /v1/models pricing)
aperture.note: Any OpenAI-compatible gateway whose /v1/models returns per-model `pricing` {input, input_cache_read, output} USD-per-token strings plus context_window_tokens. mrouter computes actual cost as usage x pricing. Point api_base at your endpoint; auth via api_key_env or api_key.

hardware.note: Unified memory (Apple Silicon). Used for memory-fit scoring: models that spill to disk page out and get slow.

routing.note: sensitive is a HARD local-only filter, not a weight: cloud models are excluded before scoring. Other use cases multiplex across local + Aperture by score (capability, speed, cost). sensitive_probability_floor: in 'auto', any prompt whose sensitive probability reaches this floor is forced local, regardless of top label.

jev.note: Jev by TypeSafe AI: System One classifier, POST /v1/systemone, $0.042/Mtok input, output free, ~70-500ms, calibrated probabilities. Optional: set TYPESAFE_API_KEY. Without a key, mrouter falls back to a local heuristic classifier at zero cost. setec_secret/setec_server are optional fields for setec-cli users; remove them if you don't use setec.

learning.note: Every routed request is logged (use case, model, latency, usage, actual cost, status). Explicit feedback (mrouter feedback / POST /v1/feedback) and observed success/latency adjust future scores by a bounded amount. Run: python3 -m mrouter learn

chat.label: General purpose chat
chat.description: Everyday assistant chat: fast, pleasant, good instruction following. Latency and cost matter; local is free.

coding.label: Coding
coding.description: Code generation, refactoring, agentic tool loops. Capability first, then context/tool-use, with a real cost term.

sensitive.label: Local inference on sensitive data
sensitive.description: LOCAL ONLY (hard filter). Rank local models by capability, RAM residency (no disk spill), context and speed.

thinking.label: Research and thinking
thinking.description: Long-form reasoning, analysis, research synthesis. Reasoning capability and long context first, cost-aware.

local-qwen3.8.notes: Local Qwen3.8 27B: strong reasoning/coding, thinking mode, hybrid linear attention. $0.

local-gemma-4.notes: Local Gemma 4 E4B: very fast, tight instruction following, vision+audio. $0.

claude-sonnet.notes: Claude Sonnet tier: near-frontier, mid-premium price.

claude-haiku.notes: Claude Haiku tier: fast and capable; check variant pricing (some are very cheap).

gpt-value.notes: GPT value tier (Terra/Luna): strong capability at low price.

deepseek-v4-pro.notes: DeepSeek V4 Pro: frontier-class reasoning/coding at a fraction of flagship price.

deepseek-v4-flash.notes: DeepSeek V4 Flash: very cheap, fast, capable. Strong value pick.

glm-flash.notes: GLM Flash/Fast tier: cheap and quick.

bench.prompt: Reply with the single word: ready

rankings.note: Optional live capability prior from Artificial Analysis. mode: curated | live | blend. Applies to cloud models only; local models keep curated + measured scores. Cache-first; degrades to curated when no key/offline.

baseten.note: Baseten decision models: elephant-1 (9B, fast) and mammoth-1 (27B, #1 of 208 on Jev Decision Index 0.4). System One API — same typed-answers shape as Jev, options sent as a named criteria map. Auth via BASETEN_API_KEY. When both are configured, decision.provider=auto prefers Baseten.

decision.note: Which categorizer 'auto' uses: auto (baseten key -> jev key -> local), baseten, jev, local. reliability_floor/min_samples: circuit breaker -- a provider whose recent classifier-attempt success rate falls below the floor over at least min_samples attempts is skipped (straight to the next provider in the chain) instead of paying its network timeout on every request. 0.0 disables the breaker.

resilience.note: Per-request resilience policy for the routing proxy (do_POST /v1/chat/completions). retry: on a retryable status, retries the SAME model up to max_attempts times with backoff_s*attempt sleep between tries. fallback: on an exhausted-retry failure (retryable status OR a connection/timeout error), cascades to the next-ranked eligible candidate (up to max_models total attempts) instead of surfacing the error -- sensitive requests only ever fall back within the local-only pool, never to cloud. circuit_breaker: an in-process (not persisted) per-model consecutive-failure counter; a model with >= failure_threshold consecutive failures is deprioritized behind every healthy candidate until cooldown_s elapses, then gets one half-open trial request. upstream_timeout_s replaces the old hardcoded 600s urlopen timeout. Every attempt (not just the final outcome) is logged to route_log.jsonl and surfaced to the client via X-Routed-Attempts. Missing block/keys default to the values shown here, so old configs stay resilient without edits.

eval.note: On-device SQLite store for custom evaluation results (benchmarks, rubric scores, LLM-judge scores, human review). Mirrors the metrics_store pattern: separate from route_log.jsonl (which also receives eval_result audit entries) and from metrics.db. Submit results via mrouter eval submit or POST /v1/eval/results. Query via mrouter eval list or GET /v1/eval/results. Supports windowed queries (1h/24h) matching the tray/dashboard metrics semantics.

metrics.note: On-device SQLite store (metrics.db, gitignored like other machine-local state) for live perf/spend metrics powering the tray app and dashboard tab: windowed p90 TTFT, p90 tokens/min, request volume, error rate, actual+estimated spend, per-model reliability/use-case breakdown. Separate from learning.log_file (route_log.jsonl), which stays the audit/learning log. windows_available controls the 1h/24h toggle in the tray/dashboard UI; default_window is used when no ?window= is given and also feeds heuristics' live-speed-score component (live_speed_min_samples requests required before live traffic overrides the bench/family speed estimate for a local model). retention_days prunes rows older than N days on a throttled schedule (every write, at most once per 5 minutes).
